_description: Real-world corporate open-source license policies, allowed licenses, prohibited (banned) licenses, and dependency restriction rules.

google.official_policy_name: Google Open Source Third-Party License Policy
google.summary: Strictly prohibits AGPL and non-commercial/ethical licenses across all backend infrastructure and client software to prevent network-copyleft contagion.
google.restricted_condition: Requires legal exception and dynamic linking verification
google.banned_rationale: AGPL requires distributing complete source code over network interfaces (SaaS), which poses catastrophic risk to proprietary backend services. Non-commercial licenses (CC-BY-NC, JSON) conflict with commercial monetization.

apache.official_policy_name: ASF Third Party License Policy (Category X Resolution)
apache.summary: Category X licenses are completely prohibited from being included or distributed in any Apache project release in source or binary form.
apache.restricted_condition: Category B: Allowed only as unaltered binary dependencies; cannot include source in repository
apache.banned_rationale: ASF releases must be freely reusable without viral copyleft obligations or field-of-use restrictions. Category X licenses contain restrictions that conflict with Apache's permissive distribution model.

meta.official_policy_name: Meta Open Source & Third-Party Code Policy
meta.summary: Prohibits AGPL, SSPL, and non-commercial licenses across all production systems, mobile applications, and backend services.
meta.restricted_condition: Requires internal Open Source Review Board (OSRB) approval
meta.banned_rationale: Forbids network-triggered source disclosure mandates and subjective ethical/non-commercial licensing terms in commercial infrastructure.

microsoft.official_policy_name: Microsoft Open Source Third-Party Use Guidelines
microsoft.summary: Bans AGPL, SSPL, and ethical clauses in commercial products and cloud services to ensure licensing integrity.
microsoft.restricted_condition: Requires Architecture & Licensing Review Board approval
microsoft.banned_rationale: Prevents reciprocal copyleft contagion into Azure backend services and commercial customer software packages.
